entities.summary: Daisuke Inoue  is a Japanese businessman best known as an inventor of the karaoke machine. Inoue, a musician in his youth employed in backing businesspeople who wanted to sing in bars, invented the machine as a means of allowing them to sing without live back-up. He did not patent the machine and so did not directly profit, but he continued to work in the industry it generated, including patenting a protective pesticide for karaoke machines. Named one of Time magazine's "Most Influential Asians of the Century" in 1999, he was awarded the Ig Nobel Peace Prize in 2004 and in 2005 was the subject of the Japanese biographical film Karaoke.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Inoue's invention of the karaoke machine had a significant impact on popular culture in East Asia, with an estimated 100 million people worldwide using the technology by the 1980s. His work also spawned a multibillion-dollar industry.
